title: The Army That Lost a War to Birds

beats.line: Australian soldiers once went to war against a flock of birds.
In 1932, thousands of emus moved into Western Australia’s wheat country.
Drought had pushed them toward food and water, and the birds tore through crops and fences.
The farmers asked the government for help.
So Australia sent Major Meredith and a few artillery soldiers with Lewis machine guns.
The plan was simple: find the flock, line up the guns, and end the problem quickly.
They were fast, spread out, and suddenly heading in every direction.
At a watering point, the army prepared a perfect ambush.
More than a thousand emus came into view. The gun jammed.
The flock scattered, and the soldiers were left chasing birds across the dust.
In the end, farmers turned to fences instead.
Australia’s strangest war was defeated by birds—and solved with better barriers.
